instructions: objstore is a Go library providing a unified file-storage interface (github.com/KARTIKrocks/objstore) across local filesystem, AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, and an in-memory backend for testing. Every backend implements the single objstore.Storage interface so application code can switch providers without changing call sites. This is a multi-module repo: root (Storage interface, shared option types, sentinel errors, LocalStorage, MemoryStorage, helpers — depends only on the stdlib and github.com/google/uuid), plus s3/, gcs/, azure/ as separate Go modules pulling in their own SDKs. Prioritize cross-backend behavioral consistency, correct error-sentinel mapping, and context/resource handling over style. See AGENTS.md for repo conventions and .greptile/rules.md for pattern rationale and worked examples from real bugs found in this codebase.

rules.rule: A behavioral change to one Storage implementation (local.go, memory.go, s3/s3.go, gcs/gcs.go, azure/azure.go) — including edge cases like boundary conditions, zero-length inputs, or error conditions — must be mirrored in the others unless the difference is explicitly justified (e.g. a capability only one provider has). Do not treat 'it matches this backend's tests' as sufficient; the whole point of the Storage interface is that callers can swap backends without their code's behavior changing.

Provider-specific errors (AWS SDK error codes, storage.ErrObjectNotExist, bloberror codes, os.IsNotExist, etc.) must be translated to the package's sentinel errors (ErrNotFound, ErrAlreadyExists, ErrInvalidPath, ErrPermission, ErrNotImplemented, ErrInvalidRange, ErrSignatureInvalid, ErrSignatureExpired) via a type-safe check (errors.As, errors.Is, or an SDK-provided predicate), never by matching on an error's string message. Flag any backend method that returns a raw provider error where a sentinel applies.

Any arithmetic that adds a caller-supplied offset and length (byte ranges, pagination bounds, buffer sizing) must not compute offset+length as an intermediate value unless it has first been bounded against a known size via subtraction (e.g. compare length against `size - offset`, not `offset + length` against `size`). Treat offset and length as adversarial int64 values that may each independently approach math.MaxInt64. This exact overflow (wrap to negative, then a slice/index panics or an SDK receives a malformed request) has been found and fixed twice in this codebase already — see .greptile/rules.md.

Every Storage method that performs I/O must accept and honor context cancellation (check ctx.Err() before starting local filesystem work; pass ctx through to every SDK call for cloud backends). Never store a context.Context in a struct field.

An io.ReadCloser, *os.File, or SDK response body/writer must be closed on every code path, including error paths reached after the resource was already acquired (e.g. an error from Stat/Seek/Read after os.Open must still close the file before returning). Prefer defer where the function returns the resource itself makes that impossible, use an explicit Close on each error branch.

A new Put/Get/List/SignedURL option must be added to the corresponding options struct (PutOptions/GetOptions/ListOptions/SignedURLOptions) and threaded through its Apply*Options helper, with any default set there — not special-cased inside a single backend's implementation.

LocalStorage resolves caller-supplied paths against BasePath on a real filesystem. Any change to path-joining or validation logic must keep rejecting paths that escape BasePath (e.g. `../`, absolute paths, symlink tricks) with ErrInvalidPath, not just handle the paths the tests happen to cover.

The root module (files directly in the repository root) must depend only on the standard library and github.com/google/uuid. A new third-party dependency belongs in a sub-module (s3/, gcs/, azure/) if anywhere — never in root go.mod.
Every new or newly-exported type, function, method, and constant must have a doc comment that starts with the identifier's own name.
